I farm 5 mu of good flat land here in Quzhou County. With the education I have, I pay close attention to what works on the North China Plain. This year, I will stick with the winter wheat–summer maize rotation that has fed my family reliably. I will sow improved wheat seed in October and harvest in early June, then immediately plant hybrid maize using no-tillage to catch the summer heat and save fuel. I will apply nitrogen, phosphate, and potash at rates I have learned give the best return—about 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu for wheat, and slightly less for maize. I will irrigate my wheat four times at critical stages and my maize twice, because groundwater is precious and I know timing matters more than flooding. For pests and weeds, I will spray three times on each crop—herbicides early, then insecticides and fungicides when the scouts tell me thresholds are reached. Rotary tillage before wheat keeps the seedbed clean, but no-tillage for maize preserves moisture and cuts costs.
